entity_types.name: Engineer
entity_types.description: A civil, structural, or mechanical engineer associated with lighthouse design, architecture, and construction.

entity_types.name: Lighthouse
entity_types.description: A marine navigational light tower or structure providing navigational aid, along with its physical and operational characteristics.

entity_types.name: Event
entity_types.description: A notable historical occurrence, operational milestone, accident, or alteration in the history of a lighthouse.

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.description: A named public authority, corporation, governing board, trust, or commercial firm associated with lighthouse management, manufacturing, or construction.

entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: A named individual, such as a lighthouse keeper, official, owner, petitioner, or notable visitor, who is not classified as an Engineer.

entity_types.name: Location
entity_types.description: A named geographic place, island, headland, waterway, or marine hazard such as a reef or rock group.

entity_types.name: Vessel
entity_types.description: A named ship, steamer, boat, or watercraft associated with navigation or maritime incidents near a lighthouse.

entity_types.name: Apparatus
entity_types.description: A specific lighting, optical, illuminant, or acoustic fog-signalling mechanism installed at or associated with a lighthouse.

fact_types.description: The lighthouse was designed, engineered, or architecturally planned by the engineer.
The historical event or operational milestone took place at or directly involved the lighthouse.
The lighthouse is physically situated on or overlooks the geographic feature or place.
The lighthouse beam or danger sector warns vessels against the maritime hazard, reef, or rock formation.
The lighthouse is managed, maintained, or monitored by the authority or organization.
The lighthouse property is owned or leased by the organization.
The lighthouse tower or facility was physically constructed by the building firm or company.
The lighthouse replaced, superseded, or succeeded an earlier lighthouse structure.
The optical, illuminant, or acoustic apparatus forms part of the lighthouse equipment.
The optical lens, burner, or signalling equipment was manufactured or supplied by the company.
The removed or decommissioned apparatus was donated, transferred, or preserved by the museum or organization.
The individual lived at, acquired, visited, inspected, or advocated for the lighthouse.
The person officiated, witnessed, or participated in the historical event.
The vessel was central to the maritime accident, wreck, or incident event.
The vessel was wrecked, grounded, or sunk at the geographic feature or reef.
The historical occurrence or disaster took place at or near the geographic location.
The physical height of the lighthouse tower above ground.
The elevation of the lighthouse light beam above sea level or high-water mark.
The operational nautical distance at which the lighthouse beam is visible.
